html:
The Third Anglo-Afghan War was a short war in May 1919 between Afghanistan and British India, which ended with Britain recognising Afghanistan's full independence in the Treaty of Rawalpindi.

Since the second war, Britain had controlled Afghan foreign policy. The new king, Amanullah Khan, declared complete independence and sent troops toward the Khyber Pass. British aircraft bombed Kabul and Jalalabad, but Britain, worn out by the First World War and unrest in India, agreed to an armistice within a month.

The treaty of 8 August 1919 gave Afghanistan control of its own foreign affairs, though it confirmed the Durand Line. Afghanistan became one of the first states to recognise Soviet Russia. Afghans celebrate their independence day each year on 19 August.
sum: The Third Anglo-Afghan War was a short war in May 1919 between Afghanistan and British India, which ended with Britain recognising Afghanistan's full independence in the Treaty of Rawalpindi.
